{"notes": "Visit 1 (ended 1:00, very early, so these are first impressions only).

Priya: Took the pad and set out a plan: a fish body with top and bottom curves running from the tail to the nose, plus a fin and tail. She delegated clearly and started the top line herself. When Tom offered to take the top line, she redirected him to the bottom line to avoid duplicate work, and asked Maya to help Leo. That is good coordination and leadership. Watch whether her switching assignments (Maya was first given the bottom line, then moved to the tail) confuses people, and whether she shares the work or holds onto the pad and the main line.

Tom: Responded fast and constructively. He volunteered for the top line, offered to continue from Priya's start, and accepted the switch to the bottom line with no friction (I only heard the offer, not his reply). Good collaboration so far. I don't yet know what he built.

Maya: Silent while I was there. She was assigned the bottom line, then reassigned to help Leo with the tail and fin. No evidence yet on her contribution, so no judgment.

Leo: Also silent. He was asked to add the fin and tail at the tail end. There is no fin or tail on the table yet, so I can't tell whether he has started.

Table state: Top and bottom body lines are both started and connected to the start. The bottom line is longer, and neither reaches the nose yet. I can't attribute individual dominoes to anyone. Next visit: check who is building what, whether the fin and tail exist, and whether the two curves meet at the nose."}
